title: Leviathan, Behemoth and Gehenna
source_text: Ἐν ᾧ ἦν διαγραφὴ κύκλων, ἀπολελυμένων μὲν ἀπ᾿ ἀλλήλων δέκα συνδουμένων δὲ ὑφ᾿ ἑνὸς κύκλου, ὃς ἐλέγετο εἶναι ἡ τῶν ὅλων ψυχὴ καὶ ὠνομάζετο Λευϊαθὰν, ὅντινα αἱ Ἰουδαίων γραφαὶ ὅ τι ποτ᾿ οὖν αἰνισσόμεναι ἔλεγον πεπλάσθαι ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ παίγνιον. ἐν γὰρ ψαλμοῖς εὕρομεν· „πάντα ἐν σοφίᾳ ἐποίησας· ἐπληρώθη ἡ γῆ τῆς κτίσεώς σου. αὕτη ἡ θάλασσα ἡ μεγάλη καὶ εὐρύχωρος· ἐκεῖ πλοῖα διαπορεύονται, ζῷα μικρὰ μετὰ μεγάλων, δράκων οὗτος, ὃν ἔπλασας ἐμπαίζειν αὐτῷ.“ ἀντὶ δὲ τοῦ „δράκων“ Λευϊαθὰν ἦν ἐν τῷ Ἑβραϊκῷ. τὸ τοίνυν ἀσεβὲς διάγραμμα τὸν σαφῶς οὕτως κατηγορηθέντα ἐν τῷ προφήτῃ Λευϊαθὰν ἔλεγεν εἶναι τὴν διὰ τῶν ὅλων πεφοιτηκυῖαν ψυχήν. εὕρομεν δ᾿ ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ τὸν Βεημὼν ὀνομαζόμενον ὡσπερεὶ τεταγμένον τινὰ μετὰ τὸν κατωτάτω κύκλον. τοῦτον δὲ τὸν Λευϊαθὰν ὁ τὸ μιαρὸν ἐκεῖνο διάγραμμα ἀναπλάσας ἐπὶ τοῦ κύκλου καὶ τοῦ κέντρου αὐτοῦ κατέγραψε, δὶς ἐκθέμενος αὐτοῦ τὸ ὄνομα. ἔτι δὲ ὁ Κέλσος μελαίνῃ γραμμῇ παχείᾳ φησὶ διειλημμένον εἶναι τὸ διάγραμμα, καὶ ταύτην ἔφασκεν εἰρῆσθαι αὐτῷ τὴν Γέενναν, οὖσαν καὶ Τάρταρον. τὴν δὲ Γέενναν ἡμεῖς ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ γεγραμμένην ὡς κολαστήριον εὑρόντες, ἐζητήσαμεν, εἴ που τῶν παλαιῶν γραμμάτων ὠνομάσθη, καὶ μάλιστα ἐπείπερ καὶ Ἰουδαῖοι χρῶνται τῷ ὀνόματι. εὕρομεν δὲ ὅπου μὲν Φάραγξ „υἱοῦ Ἐννὸμ“ ὀνομαζομένην ἐν τῇ γραφῇ, ἐν δὲ τῷ Ἑβραϊκῷ ἀντὶ τοῦ Φάραγξ μεμαθήκαμεν ὅτι κατὰ τοῦ αὐτοῦ ὑποκειμένου ἐλέγετο ἡ Φάραγξ Ἐννὸμ καὶ ἡ Γέεννα. ἐπιτηροῦντες δὲ τὰ ἀναγνώσματα εὑρίσκομεν καὶ ἐν τῷ κλήρῳ τῆς φυλῆς Βενιαμὶν τὴν Γέενναν ἢ Φάραγγα Ἐννὸμ κατειλεγμένην, οὗ ἦν καὶ Ἱερουσαλήμ. καὶ ἐξετάζοντες τὴν ἀκολουθίαν τοῦ εἶναι ἐπουράνιον Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἀπὸ τοῦ κλήρου Βενιαμὶν καὶ τῆς Φάραγγος Ἐννὸμ εὑρίσκομέν τι εἰς τὸν περὶ κολάσεων τόπον, μεταλαμβα νομένων εἰς τὴν μετὰ βασάνου κάθαρσιν τῶν τοιωνδὶ ψυχῶν κατὰ τὸ „ἰδοὺ κύριος εἰσπορεύεται ὡς πῦρ χωνευτηρίου καὶ ὡς ποία πλυνόντων· καὶ καθιεῖται χωνεύων καὶ καθαρίζων (ὡς) τὸ χρυσίον καὶ ὡς τὸ ἀργύριον“
pass_a_gloss: In which was a drawing (διαγραφή) of circles (κύκλος), ten released (ἀπολύω) from one another but bound together (συνδέω) by one circle, which was said to be the soul (ψυχή) of the whole (τὰ ὅλα) and was named Leviathan (Λευϊαθάν), whom the scriptures of the Jews, hinting (αἰνίσσομαι) at whatever they hint, said was formed (πλάσσω) by God as a plaything (παίγνιον). For in Psalms we found: 'All things in wisdom (σοφία) you made; the earth was filled with your creation (κτίσις). This the sea, the great and spacious (εὐρύχωρος); there ships pass through, small living things (ζῷα) with great, this dragon (δράκων), which you formed to mock/sport with (ἐμπαίζειν) it/him.' Instead of 'dragon' there was Leviathan in the Hebrew. So then the impious (ἀσεβής) diagram said that the Leviathan so clearly accused/condemned (κατηγορέω) in the prophet is the soul that has gone through (φοιτάω) the whole. We found in it also the one named Behemoth (Βεημώθ), as it were placed after the lowest circle. This Leviathan the one who moulded (ἀναπλάσσω) that foul (μιαρός) diagram wrote on the circle and its centre (κέντρον), setting out his name twice. Further Celsus says the diagram is divided (διαλαμβάνω) by a black thick line (γραμμή), and he said this was called by it/him Gehenna (Γέεννα), being also Tartarus (Τάρταρος). Gehenna we, having found it written in the Gospel as a place of punishment (κολαστήριον), searched whether it was named anywhere in the old writings, especially since Jews too use the name. We found it in places named in the scripture 'Valley (φάραγξ) of the son of Ennom', and in the Hebrew instead of 'Valley' we have learned that of the same subject (ὑποκείμενον) was said the Valley of Ennom and Gehenna. Watching (ἐπιτηρέω) the readings (ἀνάγνωσμα) we find also in the lot (κλῆρος) of the tribe of Benjamin Gehenna or the Valley of Ennom listed, where was also Jerusalem. And examining the sequence (ἀκολουθία) of there being a heavenly (ἐπουράνιος) Jerusalem from the lot of Benjamin and the Valley of Ennom, we find something toward the topic (τόπος) about punishments (κόλασις), souls of such kind being taken over (μεταλαμβάνω) into purification (κάθαρσις) with torment (βάσανος), according to: 'Behold the Lord enters (εἰσπορεύομαι) as fire of a smelting furnace (χωνευτήριον) and as herb (πόα) of washers; and he will sit smelting (χωνεύω) and cleansing (καθαρίζω) as the gold and as the silver.'
pass_b_english: In it was a drawing of circles, ten of them separate from one another but bound together by one circle, which was said to be the soul of the universe and was named Leviathan. Of him the Jewish Scriptures, whatever their riddle may mean, said that he was formed by God as a plaything. For in the Psalms we found: “In wisdom you have made all things; the earth is filled with your creation. Here is the great and wide sea; there ships pass through, small living things with great; this dragon, which you formed to make sport of” (Psalm 104:24–26). In place of “dragon” the Hebrew has Leviathan. So the impious diagram said that the Leviathan so plainly condemned in the prophet is the soul that pervades the universe.

We found in it also the one named Behemoth, placed, as it were, after the lowest circle. The one who devised that foul diagram wrote this Leviathan on the circle and at its centre, setting down his name twice. Further, Celsus says that the diagram was divided by a thick black line, and he said that the diagram called this line Gehenna, which is also Tartarus.

Now since we found Gehenna written in the Gospel as a place of punishment (Matthew 5:22; 10:28), we searched whether it was named anywhere in the old writings, especially since the Jews too use the name. We found that in some places Scripture calls it the “Valley of the son of Ennom” (Jeremiah 7:31–32); but in the Hebrew, as we have learned, where “Valley” stands, “the Valley of Ennom” and “Gehenna” were used of one and the same place. Keeping close watch on the readings, we find also that Gehenna, or the Valley of Ennom, is listed in the lot of the tribe of Benjamin, in which Jerusalem also lay (Joshua 18:16, 28).

And as we examine what follows from there being a heavenly Jerusalem (Hebrews 12:22), starting from the lot of Benjamin and the Valley of Ennom, we find something that bears on the teaching about punishments: souls of this kind are brought to a purification that comes through torment, according to the words, “Behold, the Lord comes in like the fire of a smelting furnace and like the washers’ lye; and he will sit smelting and purifying as gold and as silver” (Malachi 3:2–3)…

choices.choice: The Psalm is LXX Psalm 103:24–26 (English Psalm 104:24–26). Origen’s quotation runs together the LXX verses: it omits ‘how great are your works, O Lord’ (24a) and ‘there are creeping things without number’ (25), and places ‘there ships pass through’ before ‘small living things with great’; rendered as Origen gives it. ἐμπαίζειν αὐτῷ is ambiguous (to play in it, the sea; or to make sport of it/him); ‘to make sport of’ follows Origen’s own gloss παίγνιον (‘plaything’). Possible echo of Job 40:19, 29 LXX on the beast made to be mocked, not cited. ‘Condemned in the prophet’: Origen does not say which prophet; possibly the Psalmist as prophet or Isaiah 27:1 (the sword upon the dragon); left uncited. Behemoth is a name from Job 40:15, used here by the diagram, not quoted by Origen; left uncited. ‘He said that the diagram called this line Gehenna’ renders ἔφασκεν εἰρῆσθαι αὐτῷ: αὐτῷ may be the diagram or its maker; the sense is the same. Gehenna as punishment in the Gospel: Matthew 5:22, 29–30; 10:28 (also Mark 9:43–47); two representative verses cited. ‘Valley of the son of Ennom’ (φάραγξ υἱοῦ Εννομ) is LXX wording at Jeremiah 7:31–32 (also 2 Kings 23:10; Jeremiah 19:2, 6; 32:35 = LXX 39:35); Origen says ‘in some places’, so Jeremiah 7:31–32 is cited as one instance. In Benjamin’s lot LXX Joshua 18:16 has both φάραγγα Ονομ and Γαιεννα, and 18:28 lists Jebus, that is Jerusalem. The Hebrew point: gē’ (‘valley’) + Hinnom = Gehenna. ‘Heavenly Jerusalem’ cited to Hebrews 12:22 (clear allusion; Revelation 21 also possible). Malachi: Origen opens with ‘Behold, the Lord comes in’ (blending 3:1 ἰδοὺ with 3:2); LXX 3:3 has ‘as silver and as gold’, Origen ‘as gold and as silver’; Koetschau supplies (ὡς); ποία = πόα, the washers’ herb, rendered ‘lye’. τόπος in ‘the topic of punishments’ read as ‘subject/teaching’, not ‘place’. The sentence runs on into 6.26, so this chapter ends with a comma.
Valley of Ennom sentence: made Gehenna the thing named (ὀνομαζομένην) and recast the awkward 'in place of Valley ... said of the same thing' into plain English, keeping the μέν/δέ contrast
'taken over into a purification' (calque of μεταλαμβανομένων εἰς) changed to 'brought to a purification'
LXX Psalm 103 = English 104 confirmed; Malachi 3:2–3, Joshua 18:16, 28, Jeremiah 7:31–32 checked

choices.choice: 6.25: which 'prophet' condemns Leviathan is unclear (the Psalmist, or Isaiah 27:1), so no citation was added. The existing note covers it.
the Greek sentence runs on into 6.26 (καὶ κατὰ ...); the closing comma became '…' to mark the run-on; not split
